note:
Western Terrace on the 1901 census - the two households the record did not already have.

**Two of the four on this stretch are deliberately absent.** Charles Henry Clarke at 10 Western Terrace and Joseph Bright at Lincoln Villa are already in **people_1901_named_houses.json**, filed to #349 and #350. They are not repeated here, because importing both files would make every one of those fourteen people twice over.

**What that settles, though, is worth writing down.** The record carries **Lincoln Villa as the house name of 11 Western Terrace (#350)**. The 1891 enumerator wrote that household up under *Pelham Crescent*, which is why the question about it had Lincoln Villa as a name with no property. Joseph Bright is head of it in both years, so the house did not move and the name was not reused - the 1891 schedule simply carried the wrong street at its head. See [[thorn-lea-and-lincoln-villa]].

**The two households here are unfiled**, neither schedule carrying a name or a number: Edward Armitage, a lace manufacturer of 33, with his wife Margaret, a daughter, two young cousins and two servants; and Hubert A. Dowson, a solicitor of 35, with his wife Lina and two servants.

**Thorn Lea stood empty on census night** and so has no household. It held eight in 1891 under George Elinsley Coke, so it emptied between the two censuses - see [[empty-houses-census-night-1901]].
source: 1901 census enumerator's page for Western Terrace, Nottingham, transcribed by A. Hagues.
